extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images for land use and land cover classification, covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: To construct the dataset, the authors performed two steps: satellite image acquisition and dataset creation. They downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images via Amazon S3, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas and distributed over 34 European countries. They selected images with a low cloud level and extracted images recorded all over the year to increase variance. Based on the obtained satellite images, they created a dataset of 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches measuring 64x64 pixels, which were manually checked.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral Sentinel-2A satellite images provided in the Copernicus Earth observation program, downloaded via Amazon S3, associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors created 64x64 image patches from the obtained satellite images, selected 10 land use and land cover classes visible at 10 meters per pixel and frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas, and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. They did not filter samples with color cast due to atmospheric effects and let them flow into the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images with a low cloud level were selected. For comparative evaluation, RGB images were computed by combining bands B04, B03 and B02. The paper notes that the proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction. In band evaluation, bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of labeled and geo-referenced image patches. Labels were created based on 10 different land use and land cover classes chosen using the principle that they are visible at 10 meters per pixel and frequently covered by the European Urban Atlas. The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Georeferenced images distributed over 34 European countries.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the resulting classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications. Demonstrated applications include detecting land use and land cover changes, assisting in improving geographical maps, monitoring land surfaces, noticing deforestation, supporting urban area development, nature protection, sustainable development, and helping keep crowdsourced maps such as OpenStreetMap up-to-date.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The authors aimed to cover as many countries as possible and extracted images recorded all over the year to increase intra-class variance. They note low positive correlation between some classes, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The classifier sometimes confuses the agricultural land classes as well as the classes highway and river. The paper also notes that a classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark and basis for large-scale training of deep neural networks for satellite image classification and land use and land cover classification. The paper provides training and test splits for benchmarking and evaluates CNNs on the dataset. Proposed real-world applications include land use and land cover change detection and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
